# Held-out fulfillment requirements

These accepted synthetic requirements define the contract. They are independent of the tests.

## Reservation service
- Reject null/blank SKU, quantity outside 1..50, and null or nonfuture expiry with IllegalArgumentException.
- Capture the injected clock once. Expiry equal to the current instant is invalid; one millisecond later is valid.
- Normalize SKU by trimming only, preserving case. Rejected input never calls inventory.
- Query available stock with the normalized SKU. Stock equal to the requested quantity is sufficient.
- Insufficient stock raises IllegalStateException without reserving anything.
- Reserve exactly one complete Reservation with normalized SKU, quantity, the captured instant and unchanged expiry.
- Return that complete reservation. Inventory read/write failures propagate without retry or fabricated success.
- Unit tests instantiate the real service directly; the Spring annotation does not require a context.

## Quote lookup
- Use the actual MUI controls. Blank trimmed text never dispatches. A nonblank request receives trimmed text.
- The submit button remains usable during a request so a user can replace it with a newer query.
- Starting a replacement aborts the previous signal. Only the most recent request may publish a result, error or ready state.
- Display the returned quote exactly, with no prefix, suffix or stale result. Clear old output when starting work.
- A current rejection displays exactly "Lookup failed". A later retry can succeed and must clear that error.
- Unmount aborts the active request; no work is dispatched during unmount.
- Requests and settlements are controlled in tests, without sleeps, fake network or replacing the component.

## Customer profile B
Use English Given_When_Then test names and explicit Given/When/Then sections. Keep mocks at the external
inventory/lookup boundary. Preserve requirement distinctions in focused tests. Do not claim tests were run.
